viz_reviews.summary: The page renders STAR as four labelled columns read left to right with the relation names (sets up, motivates, produces) in the gaps and the PAR variant as a strip spanning Situation and Task, which is exactly the framework's shape. Facts-only leaves a coherent stated chain with the unattributed outcomes visibly loose; derived-on adds the implied objectives (Task, the idea-bearing slot, made prominent by the 1.2-size diamond and its own column), the PAR compression and the low-confidence attribution question, and grounding links land on the right facts. Metrics are clean at default view for both examples (0 overlapping pairs, 0 off-screen, 0 under cards), console is clean on load and on switching, stats lines match graph.json (13/4 nodes, 7/9/8 edges; 20/5, 10/15/14), tab switching updates data and stats both ways, and the panel shows quote plus reference for facts and rationale, confidence bar and supporting quotes for derived nodes (verified on t2, r5, p1 classic and t2, r6 tbpn). Legibility is a 4 rather than 5 because several edges run through label text (vertical chains in the Action and Situation columns, two diagonals through the tbpn Task labels) and a few labels spill past their column border; all remain readable, so nothing blocks.

notes: Research (step 2): STAR = Situation, Task, Action, Result; the behavioural-interview decomposition popularised through DDI's Targeted Selection (1970s), used for interview answers, resume bullets (PAR / CAR variants: Problem or Context, Action, Result) and performance reviews; STARR / STARL add Reflection or Learning. Situation forces the starting conditions and stakes; Task forces the actor's own objective and responsibility and is the slot most often left implicit; Action forces concrete first-person steps; Result forces a measurable outcome attributed to the action. Common misuse: 'we' instead of 'I' (agency blurred), action without result, result without attribution (post hoc), situation that swallows the answer, hypothetical instead of completed events, result that merely restates the action. Scout (step 3): three candidates returned: (1) Windsurf acquired by Cognition, told live by Jeff Wang and Scott Wu, 2025-07-14; (2) Agree.com launch to 20,000 users, Marty Ringlein, 2025-05-07; (3) Shaan Puri buying into Somewhere.com, 2025-02-13. Chose (1): a completed 72-hour event narrated by the actors themselves, an explicitly stated Task (rare; lets the graph show a fact-Task beside a derived-Task), timed Actions, measurable Results with speaker-stated attribution, corpus-central entities (Windsurf, Cognition, Google DeepMind) for the future merge, and an underserved-market reading. (2) was a close second, but its idea angle is a strategy pattern more than an underserved need. Idea-bearing slot: task. Graph (step 4): classic 17 nodes (13 fact / 4 derived), 24 edges (7 fact / 17 derived, 8 grounding); tbpn 23 nodes (20 fact / 3 derived), 37 edges (7 fact / 30 derived, 13 grounding). validate.mjs PASS, 0 errors, 0 warnings. Pilot review fixes (2026-09-09, commit content(star-par): pilot review fixes). (1) Removed tbpn t3 and t4: they were market needs, not the objective the actor owned, so they failed this README's own Task guard and put the idea layer into the Task column as nodes, which SPEC 3 now forbids. Their eight edges (e21-e24, e29-e32) went with them. Their content is carried by an idea field on t2 and, at greater length, by prose in 'Where the opportunity shows up' read from s6, s7 and r2. So that those three facts stay attached, added grounding links t2->s6 and t2->s7 (0.55) and t2->r2 (0.50), which ground the idea rather than the node text and say so in their rationales, plus two visible derived edges s6->r1 (0.50) and s7->r1 (0.55) carrying the complementarity reading t3 used to assert. (2) Fact-edge criterion (two fact endpoints plus a connective quoted from one speaker's turn): e2 (the connective is the host's question, not Wang's answer), e8 (joins Wang and the host across segments) and e9 (two host statements joined only by 'And') are now derived at 0.70 with rationales that say why. e6 and e7 were tested against the same rule and kept as fact: in both, the act and what it produced sit in one speaker's clause. Every remaining fact edge in both examples now carries source_quote and source_ref (classic: sentence numbers; tbpn: speaker plus line range); e5, e7 and e10 had their quotes extended slightly so the connective spans a real line range. (3) Every tbpn fact node and fact edge now has source_ref as 'Speaker, L<start>-L<end>', located mechanically against the transcript with the validator's own normaliser; r2's old range was wrong and is corrected to L278-L282. The transcript is not diarised, so speakers are read from surrounding turns. (4) README Example 2 restructured per SPEC 6 into 'Facts (quoted)' (fact nodes with id, label, text, quote, ref, then the fact edges with their connectives) and 'Decomposition' (derived nodes with rationale and supported-by ids, then the derived edges); 'Where the opportunity shows up' now lists the single node carrying an idea field and reads the rest from s6, s7 and r2. (5) Agency guard applied as the README states it: a1's text no longer credits Wang alone for a 'we' quote (the act stays in the node; the attribution is derived edge e40, a2->a1 at 0.70), and a4's text records that the speaker names no signatories while e13 (a3->a4, lowered from 0.85 to 0.80) carries the reading of who signed. a6 keeps its named actors because its quote was extended to 'So me and Scott and the team...', which is verbatim. classic p1 set from 0.85 to 0.80 and both p1 rationales now state what the number means in the shared band. README header uses the registry category name 'Narrative & Statement Decomposition' and the library-root link moved to the end of Related frameworks, as in toulmin-model. Engine notes, replacing the iteration-1 critic's engine-level suggestions 4 and 5 (both fixed in _meta commit 9184645): derived edges between two fact nodes now hide with the derived toggle, so the facts-only view is source-true, and the example note is a strip under the header with the camera fit accounting for it. One consequence to read as intended rather than as a defect: with derived hidden, the tbpn example keeps only 7 fact edges over 20 fact nodes, so s2 to s8, a3, r3 and r5 stand unconnected. That is what the speakers actually asserted, and the README says so under 'What the LLM added'. classic r3 has no visible edge in the default view either: the renewal figure is the one result the answer attributes to nothing, and the doubt about it is carried by the derived node r5 and its grounding link, not by an invented causal edge. README length: about 1,780 words of prose, inside SPEC 6's 1,500-3,000 cap once the mandated per-node entries, quotes, tables, mermaid and code blocks are excluded (SPEC 6 was clarified on this point in commit 9184645).
